title: Mariam al-Asturlabi: Maker of Astronomical Instruments
summary: The story of Mariam al-Asturlabi, a tenth-century craftswoman from Aleppo who built precise astronomical instruments called astrolabes, used for navigation, timekeeping, and finding prayer times.
poll: Learning a skilled craft from a parent is one of the best ways to learn.

versions.title: Mariam Builds Star Tools
versions.text:
Mariam was a skilled worker long ago. She was a girl who liked to work with her hands. She lived in Aleppo, in Syria.

Her father made a tool. It was an astrolabe. It is round. It is an instrument. It showed stars. People used it at night.

She learned the craft. She learned it in his workshop. She worked hard day by day. She did not stop till each part was just right. She learned fast.

She got very skilled. She made each astrolabe with care. Her tools helped find the right direction. The tools also told the time. They helped know when to pray.

A ruler of the city wanted her work. He asked her to make fine tools.

Not many facts about her life are known. Old books say she was skilled. They say she was good too. People still know of her work today.

versions.title: Mariam al-Asturlabi: Maker of Astronomical Instruments
versions.text:
Mariam was one of the most skilled instrument-makers of her time. She lived in Aleppo, a great city in the land we now call Syria. Workers and thinkers there worked side by side.

Her father was known in the city for making a tool called an astrolabe. It is a round instrument made of brass. It has thin plates that show the sun and stars. She learned the craft in her father's workshop, a place where skilled hands shaped fine tools by hand.

Over time, she became very good at this kind of work. She shaped each small part with care. She fit the parts just right. People used her tools to find the right direction on long trips. People also used the instrument to tell the time of day or night, and it helped them know when to pray.

Her fine work caught the notice of a powerful ruler who led her city. He wanted only the best tools for his court. He asked her to make them for him.

Very few facts about the rest of her life were ever written down. But an old book that still exists today calls her a skilled, careful maker. Today, people remember her as one of the rare named women known for this fine, exact craft.

versions.title: Mariam al-Asturlabi: A Renowned Builder of Astronomical Instruments
versions.text:
Mariam was one of the most meticulous instrument-makers of the tenth century. She was a maker whose careful work left behind some of the finest instrumentation of her time. She lived in Aleppo, in the land we now call Syria, where craft and learning both flourished.

Her father was a renowned maker of astrolabes, a device that an astronomer used to measure the sun, moon, and stars. As an apprentice in her father's busy workshop, Mariam spent years learning the exacting craft of building this instrumentation, work that demanded great care with every cut.

An astrolabe includes several thin plates, each one made for a different latitude, since the stars shift position depending on how far north or south a city lies. A meticulous maker needed careful math and steady hands to shape each plate correctly.

Mariam first learned this meticulous craft at her father's side. Later, she became renowned in her own right, surpassing many experienced makers of her generation.

Astronomers, sailors, travelers, and worshippers all depended on the fine instrumentation Mariam produced. Astronomers used her tools to study the sky. Travelers depended on them for navigation, finding direction without roads or landmarks. Worshippers used them to find the right time for prayer.

Mariam's growing reputation for meticulous work eventually reached Sayf al-Dawla, the ruler of Aleppo, who invited her to build instrumentation for his royal court, an honor given to only a few makers. Her meticulous approach set a standard that later makers in the region tried to match for many years afterward.

Scholarly records about Mariam's own personal life are scarce, since few craftsmen, especially women, were written about in detail. But an early scholarly book preserves a brief account of her skill, describing her as an outstanding maker of astrolabes. Today, Mariam's legacy endures as one of the rare named women credited with this precise and mathematical craft, and scholars still study her work as evidence of her true skill.

versions.title: Mariam al-Asturlabi: A Renowned Builder of Astronomical Instruments
versions.text:
Mariam al-Asturlabi stands among the most accomplished, meticulous, and technically gifted instrument-makers of the entire tenth century, having lived in the renowned city of Aleppo during a remarkable era when astronomy, mathematics, and precise craftsmanship flourished extensively throughout the Muslim world. Aleppo, situated in what is now Syria, was home to skilled craftsmen and vibrant, deeply interconnected scholarly circles that exchanged knowledge, tools, and refined techniques across successive generations of dedicated, disciplined practice.

Mariam's father was himself a widely renowned maker of astrolabes, a remarkably sophisticated device that astronomers relied upon extensively to measure the positions of the sun, moon, and stars with considerable, dependable accuracy. As a young apprentice within her father's busy workshop, Mariam devoted many formative years to mastering the exacting craft of designing and constructing this specialized astronomical instrumentation, demanding work that required cutting and engraving delicate metal plates with extraordinary, almost obsessive, meticulous precision.

An astrolabe typically incorporates several thin, interchangeable plates, each meticulously engraved for a distinct latitude, since the visible positions of the stars in the night sky shift considerably depending on precisely how far north or south a particular city happens to lie. Producing genuinely accurate plates demanded rigorous mathematical calculation alongside remarkably steady, practiced hands, exacting skills that ordinarily required a lengthy, demanding apprenticeship to develop fully and reliably. Mariam mastered this meticulous craft so thoroughly that she eventually surpassed many experienced craftsmen of her own generation, becoming widely and justly renowned throughout the broader region in her own right.

Astronomers, sailors, desert travelers, and worshippers alike depended heavily on the exquisite instrumentation Mariam so skillfully produced. Astronomers employed her astrolabes to study the heavens and calculate the predictable movement of the stars throughout the year, while travelers relied on them for accurate navigation, determining their precise direction even without roads or familiar landmarks nearby. Worshippers, meanwhile, used them to establish the correct times for daily prayer, calculated meticulously from the shifting position of the sun across the changing seasons.

Mariam's steadily growing reputation for meticulous precision eventually reached Sayf al-Dawla, the powerful ruler of Aleppo, who personally invited her to design and construct sophisticated astronomical instrumentation for his royal court, an honor extended to only a small, select handful of craftsmen throughout that entire era.

Scholarly records concerning Mariam's own personal life remain frustratingly scarce, since detailed record-keeping about individual craftsmen, particularly women, was uncommon throughout that historical period. Nevertheless, an early biographical dictionary preserves a brief but genuinely admiring scholarly account of her remarkable skill, describing her as an outstanding maker of astrolabes. Today, Mariam's legacy endures prominently as one of the rare named women credited with mastering this highly precise and deeply mathematical craft, a legacy that historians continue to study closely as compelling evidence of women's genuine and lasting contributions to science during the Islamic Golden Age.

HIGH.prompt: Explain why Mariam al-Asturlabi can be called a renowned and meticulous craftswoman whose legacy still matters today. Use at least three pieces of evidence from the article, and discuss both her training and the different people who used her instruments.
checklist: I explained why Mariam al-Asturlabi can be called renowned and meticulous, with at least three pieces of evidence.
I discussed both her training and the people who used her instruments.
I organized my answer in clear paragraphs with transitions such as furthermore and however.
HIGH.modelAnswer:
Mariam al-Asturlabi deserves to be called a meticulous and renowned craftswoman because of the careful, exacting way she built her astrolabes. As an apprentice in her father's workshop, she learned to engrave metal plates for different latitudes with great precision, a skill that normally took many years to master. Her reputation for this precise work eventually reached Sayf al-Dawla, the ruler of Aleppo, who invited her to build instrumentation for his royal court, a clear sign of how renowned she had become.

Furthermore, her instruments served many different kinds of people: astronomers used them to study the stars, sailors and desert travelers used them for navigation, and worshippers used them to find the correct times for prayer. However, scholarly records about the rest of her personal life are scarce, since few women craftsmen were written about in detail at that time. Even so, her legacy endures today as valuable evidence that women made genuine, meticulous contributions to science and craftsmanship during the Islamic Golden Age.
